Overall tone: upbeat on growth and employment, with inflation near the symmetric 2 percent objective and risks “roughly balanced.” This aligns with inflation-targeting goals and anchored expectations noted in the literature. The decision to raise the target range to 2–2.25 percent and signal “further gradual increases” is consistent with Taylor-rule and New Keynesian policy-rule insights (Taylor; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), as well as the Fed’s documented interest-rate smoothing behavior.

Implementation details—raising interest on reserves to 2.20 percent and setting the ON RRP at 2.00 percent—reflect floor-system operations advocated in Goodfriend (2002) and adopted since October 2008. Continued balance-sheet runoff (Treasury and MBS caps) reinforces a gradual quantitative tightening backdrop. The forward-guidance language helps anchor expectations (consistent with modern communication literature), while the rate hike and runoff can, per term-structure evidence (e.g., Cochrane and Piazzesi) and yield-curve studies, impart a modestly hawkish tilt and potential curve flattening.

Net assessment: positive macro tone (strong activity, low unemployment, stable inflation expectations) tempered by measured hawkishness (ongoing hikes and balance-sheet normalization). 

“Household spending and business fixed investment have grown strongly.”
